kinds.d: Lined box or cabinet that holds cigars at about 70% humidity; sizes run from travel cases (2-20 cigars) to cabinets (1,000-5,000).

x.d: Zino Davidoff is credited with inventing the desktop humidor, the most common home type holding about 25-500 cigars.
Desktop humidor of macassar ebony with Spanish cedar lining, built for Boveda packs and holding 50 cigars.

kinds.d: Tool for cutting the cap of a cigar, as a straight cut, punch or V-cut.

x.d: Teardrop-shaped double guillotine, opening by button; sold in several styles including Xi2 and Xi3.
Rosewood-sided cutter making both straight and V-cuts.

kinds.d: Case for carrying cigars on the person, usually leather or metal.
Device that keeps humidor humidity near 70%: propylene glycol solution, silica gel beads, electronic or two-way pack.

x.d: Packet giving six months of maintenance-free humidification at 69% RH (size 320), with seasoning packets.

kinds.d: Gauge showing humidity inside a humidor; analog and digital types, digital described as more accurate.

brands.d: Maker of cigar cutters including the Xi line, and of cases.
Maker of two-way humidity-control packs and a Boveda humidor.
Swiss house credited with the desktop humidor.
Solingen cutlery maker credited with a dual-ended cigar cutter.
